title: Caporossi–Cioabă–Gutman–Hansen conjecture on minimum-energy connected graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph with $n$ vertices and $e$ edges. For a graph with adjacency eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n$, its energy is $E(G)=\sum_{i=1}^n|\lambda_i|$. Let $S_{n,e}$ be the graph obtained from the star $S_n$ by adding $e-n+1$ edges all incident with the same vertex, and let $B_{n,e}$ be the bipartite $(n,e)$-graph with two vertices in one part, one of which is adjacent to every vertex in the other part. **Caporossi–Cioabă–Gutman–Hansen conjecture.** For $n\geq 6$ and $n-1\leq e\leq 2(n-2)$, the connected graphs with minimum energy are $S_{n,e}$ when $e\leq n+\left[\frac{n-7}{2}\right]$, and $B_{n,e}$ otherwise. This conjecture concerns the extremal energy of connected graphs across a broad range of edge counts; the supplied text gives no evidence resolving it.
source_name: Hongping Ma and Yongqiang Bai, “On the minimal energy of tetracyclic graphs”, arXiv:1408.1283 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.1283

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2014).

title: Ratner's non-divergence conjecture for unipotent flows
statement:
Let $G$ be a Lie group, let $\Gamma$ be a discrete subgroup of $G$, let $\{u_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}\subseteq G$ be a unipotent one-parameter subgroup, and let $x=g\Gamma\in G/\Gamma$. For a neighborhood $N$ of the identity in $G$, consider the set of times at which the conjugated subgroup intersects $N$ nontrivially. **Ratner's non-divergence conjecture.** For any point $x=g\Gamma\in G/\Gamma$, there exists a neighborhood $N$ of the identity in $G$ such that

$$
\frac{1}{T}m\bigl(\{t\in[0,T]:N\cap(u_tg)\Gamma(u_tg)^{-1}\neq\{e\}\}\bigr)<\epsilon
$$

for all large $T>0$, where $m$ is Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$. This conjecture asks for quantitative non-divergence of unipotent flows for arbitrary discrete subgroups, extending the known results for lattices and related settings; its resolution is not specified in the source.
source_name: C. Davis Buenger and Cheng Zheng, “Non-Divergence of Unipotent Flows on Quotients of Rank One Semisimple Groups”, arXiv:1408.2591 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.2591

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2014).

title: Homological critical-probability conjecture for hyperbolic percolation
statement:
Let $G(m)$ be the hyperbolic graph considered in the paper, let $p_c$ denote its critical probability, and let

$$
p_h=\frac{}{ }\sup\left\{p\in[0,1/2]\mid D(p)+p-\frac{2}{m}=0\right\},
$$

where $D(p)$ is the rank difference function defined from the limiting homological dimensions of random subgraphs at parameters $p$ and $1-p$. **Homological critical-probability conjecture.** For $m\geq 5$,

$$
p_c=p_h.
$$

The preceding theorem proves that $p_h$ is an upper bound for $p_c$. Equality would identify the homological threshold with the percolation threshold in the genuinely hyperbolic, non-amenable case and would also determine the corresponding threshold relevant to hyperbolic surface codes.
source_name: Nicolas Delfosse and Gilles Zémor, “A homological upper bound on critical probabilities for hyperbolic percolation”, arXiv:1408.4031 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.4031

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2014).

title: Unit-circle roots conjecture for the Goldbach polynomials
statement:
For each positive integer $N$, let $F_N$ be the polynomial defined from the indicator function of the odd primes by

$$
F_N(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\left(\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}\chi_{\mathcal P}(n)z^{kn}\right)^2.
$$

Let $\varphi$ denote Euler's totient function. **Unit-circle roots conjecture for the Goldbach polynomials.** If $N>5$ is an integer, then $F_N$ has precisely $2\varphi(N)$ roots on the unit circle. The paper presents this as a strengthening of Goldbach's conjecture, supported by numerical evidence; the cyclotomic divisibility results already guarantee the stated minimum number of unit-circle roots.
source_name: Peter B. Borwein, Stephen K. K. Choi, Greg Martin and Charles L. Samuels, “Polynomials whose reducibility is related to the Goldbach conjecture”, arXiv:1408.4881 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.4881

title: Cycle-count conjecture for degree 3-critical graphs
statement:
A **degree 3-critical graph** is a graph on $n$ vertices with $2n-2$ edges and no proper induced subgraph of minimum degree $3$. **Cycle-count conjecture.** Every degree $3$-critical graph on $n$ vertices contains cycles of at least

$$
3\log_2 n+O(1)
$$

distinct lengths. The conjecture is motivated by the Bollobás–Brightwell construction, which gives degree $3$-critical graphs with no cycles longer than $4\log_2 n+O(1)$. Determining the minimum possible number of distinct cycle lengths remains open.
source_name: Lothar Narins, Alexey Pokrovskiy and Tibor Szabó, “Graphs without proper subgraphs of minimum degree 3 and short cycles”, arXiv:1408.5289 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.5289

title: Threshold conjecture for the index of squarefree powers of edge ideals
statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $I$ be its edge ideal, and let $I^{[k]}$ denote its $k$th squarefree power. Let $\nu_0(G)$ be the maximum size of a restricted matching in $G$, with $\nu_0(G)=1$ if no restricted matching exists. **Squarefree-power threshold conjecture.**

$$
\index(I^{[k]})>1\quad\text{if and only if}\quad k\geq\nu_0(G).
$$

The preceding lemma proves $\index(I^{[k]})=1$ for $0<k<\nu_0(G)$, while the paper notes that the asserted direction at and above the threshold is proved for cycles but remains open for general simple graphs.
source_name: Mina Bigdeli, Juergen Herzog and Rashid Zaare-Nahandi, “On the index of powers of edge ideals”, arXiv:1408.5475 (2021).

title: A linear bound for real critical points of Fermat hypersurfaces
statement:
Let $F_{n,d}$ be the Fermat hypersurface, and let $u\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ be a point for which the squared distance function has finitely many critical points. The real critical points are the real solutions of the critical equation for the squared distance function on $F_{n,d}$.

**Linear-bound conjecture.** The number of real critical points of the critical equation is at most

$$
2n-1.
$$

The preceding theorem gives a bound independent of $d$, while the sharp bound is known only in the case $n=1$, where there is one real solution. For $n=2$ the maximum appears to be $3$, but no proof is known, and higher-dimensional cases remain open.
source_name: Hwangrae Lee, “The Euclidean Distance Degree of Fermat Hypersurfaces”, arXiv:1409.0684 (2015).
references:

title: Articulated Zilber-Pink conjecture for mixed Shimura and semi-abelian varieties
statement:
Let $X$ be a mixed Shimura variety or a semi-abelian variety defined over $\mathbb{C}$. Let $\langle A\rangle$ denote the smallest special subvariety containing a subvariety $A$, and define its defect by

$$
\delta(A)=\dim\langle A\rangle-\dim A.
$$

For $T\in\mathcal{S}_X$, $V\subseteq T$, and a non-negative integer $\delta$, let ${\rm Atyp\,}^{\delta}(V,T)$ be the union of subvarieties $A\subseteq V$ with $\delta(A)\leq\delta$. **Articulated Zilber-Pink conjecture.** The set ${\rm Atyp\,}^{\delta}(V,T)$ is a finite union of atypical subvarieties of defect at most $\delta$. The source explains that this is a stronger, defect-by-defect formulation implied formally by Zilber-Pink; the supplied text does not state that either conjecture is resolved.
source_name: Philipp Habegger and Jonathan Pila, “O-minimality and certain atypical intersections”, arXiv:1409.0771 (2014).
references:

title: Defect condition for mixed Shimura varieties and weakly special subvarieties
statement:
Let $X$ be a mixed Shimura variety, and let $A\subseteq B\subseteq X$ be subvarieties. Write $\langle A\rangle$ and $\langle B\rangle$ for their smallest special subvarieties and $\langle A\rangle_{\rm geo}$ and $\langle B\rangle_{\rm geo}$ for their smallest weakly special subvarieties. Define

$$
\delta(A)=\dim\langle A\rangle-\dim A,
\qquad
\delta_{\rm geo}(A)=\dim\langle A\rangle_{\rm geo}-\dim A.
$$

**Defect condition.** Every mixed Shimura variety, and every weakly special subvariety, has the defect condition. The supplied span does not give the formal definition of the defect condition or state whether this claim is open, so the precise intended assertion requires checking against the surrounding source.

title: Balogh–Barát–Gerbner–Gyárfás–Sárközy cycle-partition conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with a red-blue coloring of its edges. A partition into cycles is a collection of vertex-disjoint monochromatic cycles spanning $V(G)$.

**Balogh–Barát–Gerbner–Gyárfás–Sárközy conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(G)>\frac{3n}{4},
$$

then $G$ has a partition into a red cycle and a blue cycle.

This is the minimum-degree analogue of Lehel's conjecture for complete graphs. The paper proves the result under the asymptotically weaker condition $\delta(G)>(3/4+o(1))n$, while the exact threshold stated here remains open in the source.
source_name: Louis DeBiasio and Luke Nelsen, “Monochromatic cycle partitions of graphs with large minimum degree”, arXiv:1409.1874 (2016).
references:

title: Open Virasoro conjecture for the full open partition function
statement:
Let $F^c$ and $F^o$ be the closed and open descendent generating series, and define the full partition function by

$$
\mathsf{Z}=\exp(F^c+F^o).
$$

Let $L_n$ be the differential operators in $u$ and the variables $t_i$, and define, for $n\geq -1$,

$$
\mathcal{L}_n=L_n+u^n s\frac{\partial^{n+1}}{\partial s^{n+1}}+\frac{3n+3}{4}u^n\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n}.
$$

**Open Virasoro conjecture.** The operators $\mathcal{L}_n$ annihilate the full partition function:

$$
\forall n\geq -1,\qquad \mathcal{L}_n\mathsf{Z}=0.
$$

These constraints extend the closed Virasoro constraints to the open theory and are intended to determine the open descendent invariants. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence.
source_name: Rahul Pandharipande, Jake P. Solomon and Ran J. Tessler, “Intersection theory on moduli of disks, open KdV and Virasoro”, arXiv:1409.2191 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.2191

title: Oblak's recursive conjecture for generic commuting nilpotent Jordan types
statement:
Let $P$ be a partition, let $\mathcal D_P$ be the associated poset, and let $C_a$ be a maximum-length U-chain in $\mathcal D_P$. Removing $C_a$ gives a partition $P'(P,a)$; recursively define $Ob(P)=(|C_a|,Ob(P'))$, with $Ob(P)=(n)$ when $P$ is almost rectangular. **Oblak's recursive conjecture.** The generic nilpotent Jordan-type map satisfies

$$
\mathfrak Q(P)=Ob(P).
$$

The source states that this conjecture appears close to resolved and cites subsequent work, but the supplied status is unknown; it is therefore recorded as open here.
source_name: Anthony Iarrobino, Leila Khatami, Bart Van Steirteghem and Rui Zhao, “Nilpotent matrices having a given Jordan type as maximum commuting nilpotent orbit”, arXiv:1409.2192 (2018).

title: The intermediate-word length conjecture for K-Knuth equivalent tableaux
statement:
Let $T$ and $T'$ be tableaux with $T\equiv T'$. For a tableau $T$, let its **size** be the number of boxes in its shape, and let $w\overset{k}{\equiv}w'$ mean that $w$ and $w'$ can be connected by $K$-Knuth moves through words of length at most $k$. **Intermediate-word length conjecture.** If $k$ is the largest size of a tableau $K$-Knuth equivalent to $T$ or $T'$, then

$$
\mathfrak{row}(T)\overset{k}{\equiv}\mathfrak{row}(T').
$$

The theorem proved immediately beforehand gives a weaker polynomial upper bound, while this conjecture asserts that the maximum tableau size in the equivalence class suffices. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source_name: Christian Gaetz, Michelle Mastrianni, Rebecca Patrias, Hailee Peck, Colleen Robichaux, David Schwein and Ka Yu Tam, “K-Knuth Equivalence for Increasing Tableaux”, arXiv:1409.6659 (2015).

title: The treewidth upper-bound conjecture for line graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $L(G)$ be its line graph, let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree, and let $\textsf{tw}(G)$ denote its treewidth. **The treewidth upper-bound conjecture.** One has

$$
\textsf{tw}(L(G)) \leq \tfrac{1}{2}(\textsf{tw}(G)+1)\Delta(G) - 1.
$$

This is presented as the strongest possible improvement of the preceding upper bound in terms of maximum degree and treewidth. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
source_name: Daniel J. Harvey and David R. Wood, “The Treewidth of Line Graphs”, arXiv:1409.6810 (2014).

title: The algebraic-curve conjecture for functions over finite fields
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $f:{\rm GF}(p)\to{\rm GF}(p)$, and let $I(f)$ denote the minimum defined by

$$
I(f)=\min\left\{i+j:\sum_{x\in{\rm GF}(p)}x^j f(X)^i\neq 0\right\}.
$$

Let $\epsilon$ and $t$ be as in the stated hypothesis. **The algebraic-curve conjecture.** If

$$
I(f)>\frac{p-1-2\epsilon}{t}+t-2+\epsilon
$$

for some integer $t$, then the graph of $f$ is contained in an algebraic curve of degree $t-1$.
This conjecture proposes an algebraic strengthening of the preceding direction theorem, replacing its conclusion about the number of points on each line by containment in a low-degree curve; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
source_name: Jan De Beule, “Direction problems in affine spaces”, arXiv:1409.6960 (2014).
references:

title: McDiarmid–Mohar conjecture on acyclic chromatic number of oriented graphs
statement:
Let $D$ be an **oriented graph**, meaning that at most one directed edge joins any pair of vertices. Write $\bar{\Delta}(D)$ for its average maximum degree and let $\chi_A(D)$ denote its acyclic chromatic number.

**McDiarmid–Mohar conjecture.** Every oriented graph $D$ satisfies

$$
\chi_A(D) = O\left(\frac{\bar{\Delta}(D)}{\log \bar{\Delta}(D)}\right).
$$

This conjecture predicts a logarithmic improvement over the greedy bound $\chi_A(D)\leq \bar{\Delta}(D)+1$, in analogy with strong upper bounds for chromatic number in undirected graphs. The source presents it as an open conjecture attributed to McDiarmid and Mohar.
source_name: Noah Golowich, “The m-Degenerate Chromatic Number of a Digraph”, arXiv:1409.7535 (2018).
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2014). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1110.4896](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.4896), [arXiv:1110.4898](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.4898).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.7535

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

title: Extension of the McDiarmid–Mohar bound to m-degenerate chromatic number
statement:
Let $m$ be a positive integer, let $c$ be a constant independent of $m$, and let $D$ be an oriented graph. Write $\bar{\Delta}(D)$ for its average maximum degree and let $\chi_m(D)$ denote its $m$-degenerate chromatic number.

**m-degenerate extension conjecture.** Every oriented graph $D$ satisfies

$$
\chi_m(D) \leq (c+o(1))\frac{\bar{\Delta}(D)/m}{\log(\bar{\Delta}(D)/m)}.
$$

This conjecture extends the proposed logarithmic improvement for acyclic chromatic number to the $m$-degenerate chromatic number. The source proves a bound differing from the corresponding acyclic conjecture by a factor of $\log \bar{\Delta}(D)$ and states that a new technique would be needed to obtain the conjectured logarithmic factor.
source_name: Noah Golowich, “The m-Degenerate Chromatic Number of a Digraph”, arXiv:1409.7535 (2018).

title: The generalized-star path-packing conjecture in hypercubes
statement:
Let $Q_k$ be the $k$-dimensional hypercube, and let $P_j(Q_k)$ denote the relevant maximum number of paths in the paper's generalized-star construction. Define

$$
\mathcal{E}(n)=\sum_{k=2}^{\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor}\binom{n}{k},\qquad \mathcal{O}(n)=2^n-\mathcal{E}(n)-1.
$$

**The generalized-star path-packing conjecture.** Let

$$
a=\left\lfloor\frac{\mathcal{E}(n)}{j}\right\rfloor,\qquad b=\left\lfloor\frac{\mathcal{O}(n)}{j}\right\rfloor.
$$

If $\min\{a,b\}=b$, then $P_j(Q_k)=2b$; otherwise, $P_j(Q_k)=2a+1$. The surrounding text does not establish the precise definition of $P_j(Q_k)$ or resolve this conjecture.
source_name: Kavish Gandhi and Chiheon Kim, “Saturation Number of Trees in the Hypercube”, arXiv:1409.7983 (2014).
references:

title: The rectilinear crossing-number formula for complete tripartite graphs
statement:
Let $n_1,n_2,n_3\geq 1$, and let $K_{n_1,n_2,n_3}$ be the complete tripartite graph with part sizes $n_1,n_2,n_3$. Its rectilinear crossing number, denoted by $\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(K_{n_1,n_2,n_3})$, is the minimum number of crossings in a drawing in which every edge is a straight line segment. Let $A(n_1,n_2,n_3)$ be the upper-bound expression defined in the paper.

**Rectilinear crossing-number conjecture.**

$$
\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(K_{n_1,n_2,n_3})=A(n_1,n_2,n_3).
$$

The preceding upper and lower bounds provide evidence for this formula, which is known in several cases where two parts are small but remains open in general.
source_name: Ellen Gethner, Leslie Hogben, Bernard Lidický, Florian Pfender, Amanda Ruiz and Michael Young, “Crossing numbers of complete tripartite and balanced complete multipartite graphs”, arXiv:1410.0720 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.0720

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2014).

title: The crossing-number equality conjecture for complete tripartite graphs
statement:
Let $n_1,n_2,n_3\geq 1$, and let $K_{n_1,n_2,n_3}$ be the complete tripartite graph with part sizes $n_1,n_2,n_3$. Write $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ for the crossing number of a graph $G$, and $\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(G)$ for its rectilinear crossing number, the minimum number of crossings in a straight-line drawing of $G$.

**Crossing-number equality conjecture.**

$$
\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(K_{n_1,n_2,n_3})=\operatorname{cr}(K_{n_1,n_2,n_3}).
$$

Since every rectilinear drawing is a planar drawing, the left-hand side is always at least the ordinary crossing number. The conjecture asserts that complete tripartite graphs always admit optimal straight-line drawings; the supplied context gives evidence from the preceding bounds but no resolution.
source_name: Ellen Gethner, Leslie Hogben, Bernard Lidický, Florian Pfender, Amanda Ruiz and Michael Young, “Crossing numbers of complete tripartite and balanced complete multipartite graphs”, arXiv:1410.0720 (2014).

title: Xu's polynomial-time conjecture for the maximum forcing number of elementary polyominoes
statement:
Let $G$ be an **elementary polyomino**, meaning a polyomino whose associated plane bipartite graph is elementary. The **maximum forcing number conjecture.** The maximum forcing number of $G$ can be computed in polynomial time.

This conjecture extends the polynomial-time result known for elementary hexagonal systems to elementary polyominoes. The paper's abstract indicates that it proves the claim, showing that the maximum forcing number of an elementary polyomino equals its Clar number and can therefore be computed in polynomial time.
source_name: Liqiong Xu, Yuqing Lin and Fuji Zhang, “The maximum forcing number of polyomino”, arXiv:1410.0747 (2014).

title: Equitable induced-forest partition conjecture for bounded-degree graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$. An **equitable partition** is a partition of the vertex set into parts whose sizes differ by at most one, and an **induced forest** is a vertex-induced subgraph that is a forest. **Equitable induced-forest partition conjecture.** For any integers $\Delta$ and $k\geqslant\left\lceil\frac{\Delta+1}{2}\right\rceil$, every graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ can be equitably partitioned into $k$ induced forests. The provided excerpt does not state whether this conjecture has been resolved, so its status remains open here.
source_name: Louis Esperet, Laetitia Lemoine and Frédéric Maffray, “Equitable partition of graphs into induced forests”, arXiv:1410.0861 (2015).

title: de Freitas–Nikiforov–Patuzzi conjecture on the Q-index of graphs forbidding even cycles
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, and let $q(G)$ be the largest eigenvalue of its signless Laplacian. Let $S_{n,k}=K_k\vee\overline{K}_{n-k}$, and let $S_{n,k}^{+}$ be obtained from $S_{n,k}$ by adding an edge.

**de Freitas–Nikiforov–Patuzzi conjecture.** For $k\geq 2$ and a graph $G$ of sufficiently large order $n$, if $G$ has no cycle of length $2k+1$, then

$$
q(G)<q(S_{n,k}),
$$

unless $G=S_{n,k}$. If $G$ has no cycle of length $2k+2$, then

$$
q(G)<q(S_{n,k}^{+}),
$$

unless $G=S_{n,k}^{+}$.

The paper states that its results complete the proof of this conjecture, so both assertions are solved.
source_name: Vladimir Nikiforov and Xiying Yuan, “Maxima of the Q-index: forbidden even cycles”, arXiv:1410.2142 (2014).
references:

title: Continuity of the connective constant under local convergence
statement:
Let $G$ be an infinite transitive connected graph, and let $\{G_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of infinite transitive connected graphs that converges locally to $G$. For each graph, let $\mu(G)$ denote its connective constant, defined as the exponential growth rate of the number of self-avoiding walks.

**Continuity conjecture.** The connective constant is continuous with respect to local convergence:

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(G_n)=\mu(G).
$$

The connective constant governs the exponential growth of self-avoiding walks and is known explicitly for very few graphs. Continuity under local convergence would allow connective constants of locally approximating transitive graphs to determine that of the limit; the source provides no resolution of this assertion.
source_name: He Song, Kai-Nan Xiang and Song-Chao-Hao Zhu, “Connective Constants on Cayley Graphs”, arXiv:1410.2591 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.2591

title: Non-realizability of powers of the exceptional 2-pairing
statement:
Let $\mathcal{E}_{2^r}$ denote the exceptional pairing on the cyclic group of order $2^r$, as used in the paper. For an integer $k\geq 1$, consider the direct product of $k$ copies of this paired group. **Non-realizability conjecture for the exceptional pairing.** For any $k\geq 1$, there is no graph $G$ such that

$$
\operatorname{Jac}(G)\simeq(\mathcal{E}_{2^r})^k.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the proved non-realizability of $(\mathcal{E}_2)^k$ and by the authors' failure to find any graph realizing $\mathcal{E}_{2^r}$. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
source_name: Louis Gaudet, David Jensen, Dhruv Ranganathan, Nicholas Wawrykow and Theodore Weisman, “Realization of groups with pairing as Jacobians of finite graphs”, arXiv:1410.5144 (2017).

title: The lower-order finite p-group cycle map conjecture
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number and let $K$ be a finite $p$-group of order less than $p^{p+3}$. The mod $p$ cycle map

$$
cl:CH^2BK/p\to H^4(BK)
$$

**Cycle map conjecture.** The map $cl$ is injective.

This conjecture proposes that the smallest finite $p$-groups for which the mod $p$ cycle map fails to be injective have order at least $p^{p+3}$. The paper establishes non-injectivity for a group of order $p^{p+3}$, while the asserted lower bound remains open.
source_name: Masaki Kameko, “On the cycle map of a finite group”, arXiv:1410.5178 (2016).

title: Existence of a subforest preserving game chromatic number
statement:
Let $F$ be a forest, and let $\F'\subseteq F$ be a subforest. Write $\Delta(F')$ for its maximum degree and $\chi_{\rm g}(F')$ for its game chromatic number.

**Subforest preservation conjecture.** There exists a subforest $F'\subseteq F$ such that

$$
\Delta(F')\leq \chi_{\rm g}(F)
$$

and

$$
\chi_{\rm g}(F')=\chi_{\rm g}(F).
$$

The conjecture would reduce the study of the game chromatic number of forests to subforests whose maximum degree is bounded by the original game chromatic number. It is stated in the conclusions as an open question; the preceding results provide classification criteria in some degree-restricted cases but do not establish the claim in general.
source_name: Charles Dunn, Victor Larsen, Kira Lindke, Troy Retter and Dustin Toci, “The game chromatic number of trees and forests”, arXiv:1410.5223 (2014).

title: Full $L^2$-Alexander torsion conjecture for monodromy dilatation
statement:
Let $K$ be a fibered oriented knot with monodromy $f$, and normalize its full $L^2$-Alexander torsion so that $\tau^{(2)}(K)(1)=1$. **Full $L^2$-Alexander dilatation conjecture.** Then

$$
\sup\left\{T\in\mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0}\mid \tau^{(2)}(K)(t)\big|_{(0,T)}\text{ is constant}\right\}=\exp(-h(f)),
$$

where $h(f)$ is the entropy of the monodromy.

Thus the first transition point of the normalized full $L^2$-Alexander torsion would determine the monodromy dilatation. The source presents this as an open conjecture.
source_name: Jérôme Dubois, Stefan Friedl and Wolfgang Lück, “Three flavors of twisted invariants of knots”, arXiv:1410.6924 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.6924

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2014). “We refer to for various other conjectures and open questions regarding the twisted Alexander torsion of hyperbolic knots.”

title: General upper-bound conjecture for interval cyclic colorings
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with at least two vertices, let $V(G)$ be its vertex set, and let $\mathfrak{N}_{c}$ denote the class of interval cyclically colorable graphs. Write $W_c(G)$ for the maximum number of colors in an interval cyclic coloring. **The general interval cyclic upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
W_c(G)\leq 2\lvert V(G)\rvert-3.
$$

This conjecture proposes removing the maximum-degree term from the previously proved general bound for connected interval cyclically colorable graphs. The paper also relates it to the triangle-free case, but does not establish either conjecture.
source_name: Petros A. Petrosyan and Sargis T. Mkhitaryan, “Interval cyclic edge-colorings of graphs”, arXiv:1411.0290 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.0290

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2014).

title: Conjecture on the six smallest inversion numbers
statement:
For a fixed positive integer $b$, let $\operatorname{inv}(a,b)$ denote the inversion number and let $I_n(b)$ be its $n$th smallest value, where $1\leq n\leq6$. **Six-smallest-values conjecture.** For $1\leq n\leq6$, one has

$$
I_n(b)\geq\frac{(n-1)(b+1)(b+1-n)}{4n},
$$

with equality

$$
\operatorname{inv}(n,b)=\frac{(n-1)(b+1)(b+1-n)}{4n}
$$

when $b\equiv-1\pmod n$. This extends the proved bounds for the second smallest and second largest values to a conjectural description of the six smallest inversion numbers; the source does not indicate that the full statement has been resolved.
source_name: Yiwang Chen, Nicholas Dunn, Campbell Hewett and Shashwat Silas, “On the Inversion Polynomial for Dedekind Sums”, arXiv:1411.4092 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.4092

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).

title: Alon–Frankl conjecture on comparable pairs above the square-root threshold
statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of $m$ subsets of $[n]$, and let $c(n,m)$ be the maximum number of comparable pairs in a family of $m$ subsets of $[n]$. **Alon–Frankl conjecture.** If

$$
m=n^{\omega(1)}2^{n/2},
$$

then

$$
c(n,m)=o(m^2).
$$

This conjecture refines Erdős's question about whether $m=\omega(2^{n/2})$ implies $c(n,m)=o(m^2)$, but the paper's abstract states that it resolves the conjecture by proving the displayed conclusion.
source_name: Noga Alon, Shagnik Das, Roman Glebov and Benny Sudakov, “Comparable pairs in families of sets”, arXiv:1411.4196 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.4196

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of November 2014); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Universal upper bound conjecture for slack matrices of polygons
statement:
Let $S_n$ be the slack matrix of any $n$-gon, and let $\lfloor x\rfloor$ denote the largest integer not exceeding $x$. **Polygon slack-matrix upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{rank}_+(S_n)\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n+6}{2}\right\rfloor,
$$

and equality holds for $5\leq n\leq15$. The conjecture is motivated by computational experiments on generic polygons; the source reports no proof or disproof.
source_name: Arnaud Vandaele, Nicolas Gillis, François Glineur and Daniel Tuyttens, “Heuristics for Exact Nonnegative Matrix Factorization”, arXiv:1411.7245 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.7245

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2014).

title: Maximum-transcendentality conjecture for loop amplitudes
statement: Consider an $L$-loop amplitude in dimensional regularisation with $D=4-2\epsilon$, and write its Laurent expansion in $epsilon$. **Maximum-transcendentality conjecture.** The Laurent coefficient of $epsilon^k$ contains terms of weight at most $2L+k$. The source notes that only a few theorems establish such weight bounds for specific classes of loop integrals, so the generic statement remains conjectural.
source_name: Claude Duhr, “Mathematical aspects of scattering amplitudes”, arXiv:1411.7538 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.7538

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).

title: Garijo et al.'s locating-dominating set conjecture for twin-free graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a twin-free graph of order $n$ without isolated vertices. A **locating-dominating set** is a dominating set $D$ such that every two distinct vertices outside $D$ have distinct neighborhoods in $D$; let $gamma_L(G)$ denote the minimum cardinality of a locating-dominating set of $G$.

**Garijo et al.'s conjecture.** Every twin-free graph $G$ of order $n$ without isolated vertices satisfies

$$
\gamma_L(G)\leq \frac{n}{2}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a universal upper bound on the locating-dominating number of twin-free graphs. The supplied source does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.
source_name: Florent Foucaud, Michael A. Henning, Christian Löwenstein and Thomas Sasse, “Locating-dominating sets in twin-free graphs”, arXiv:1412.2376 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.2376

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2014).

title: Conjecture on the largest prime divisor of rank-proportion denominators
statement: Let $c_k$ be the limiting proportion of vertices of rank $k$, and let $denom(c_k)$ denote its denominator when $c_k$ is written in lowest terms. **Denominator prime-divisor bound conjecture.** The largest prime divisor of $denom(c_k)$ is at most as large as some relatively slowly growing function of $k$, possibly $2^{k+1}+1$. The authors motivate this conjecture with the observed factorizations for $k\leq 5$, but the precise slowly growing function is not specified.
source_name: Miklos Bona and Boris Pittel, “On a random search tree: asymptotic enumeration of vertices by distance from leaves”, arXiv:1412.2796 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.2796

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2014).

title: Cubic prime-divisor conjecture for sparsely Schemmel totient numbers
statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer, let $n>1$ be an integer with $n\in F_r$, and let $P_1(n)$ denote the smallest prime divisor of $n$. **Cubic prime-divisor conjecture.**

$$
P_1(n)^3\nmid n.
$$

This generalizes the result of Masser and Shiu that $P_1(n)^3\nmid n$ for sparsely totient numbers. The supplied context proves the weaker assertion that $P_1(n)^4\nmid n$ for sufficiently large $n\in F_r$, while the stated cubic-divisibility claim remains open.
source_name: Colin Defant, “On Sparsely Schemmel Totient Numbers”, arXiv:1412.3080 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.3080

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2014).

title: Disjointness minimizes the number of simultaneous splitters
statement: Let $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, and let a **splitter** of a collection of subsets be a subset that splits every member of the collection. **Disjoint-hardest conjecture.** Let $B_1,\ldots,B_n$ be a collection of subsets of $[k]$. Then the number of splitters of $B_1,\ldots,B_n$ is minimized when the collection is pairwise disjoint. If true, this would yield an upper bound of $O(g(n)k^{n/2+1})$ for the minimum size of an $n$-splitting family over $[k]$; the analogous statement is proved in the paper for configurations of two sets, while the general case remains open.
source_name: Daniel Condon, Samuel Coskey, Luke Serafin and Cody Stockdale, “On generalizations of separating and splitting families”, arXiv:1412.4683 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.4683

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2014).

title: The generic-and-Hilton–Milner obstruction conjecture for EKR in random hypergraphs
statement:
Let ${\cal H}$ be the random $k$-uniform hypergraph with edge-probability $\varphi$, let $\Delta$ denote its maximum degree, and let $\Lambda'(\Delta)$ be the parameter from Theorem~. Assume that

$$
\Lambda'(\Delta)<o(1)\quad\text{a.s.}
$$

and that ${\cal H}$ almost surely does not contain a Hilton–Milner family of size $\Delta$. **Generic-and-Hilton–Milner obstruction conjecture.** Under these assumptions, ${\cal H}$ almost surely satisfies the Erdős–Ko–Rado property.
source_name: Arran Hamm and Jeff Kahn, “On Erdős-Ko-Rado for random hypergraphs I”, arXiv:1412.5085 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5085

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2014).

title: The folklore sup-norm conjecture for newforms with mildly ramified central character
statement:
Let $f$ be a newform on $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ with level $M$ and conductor $N$, and let $N_1$ be the smallest integer such that $N\mid N_1^2$. Assume that $M\mid N_1$. **The folklore sup-norm conjecture.** One has

$$
\frac{\|f\|_\infty}{\|f\|_2} \ll_{\lambda/k,\varepsilon} N^{\varepsilon}.
$$

This conjecture asserts the expected essentially optimal sup-norm bound when the central character is not too highly ramified; the paper explains that it would follow from the absence of global obstructions beyond local ones, together with the local conjecture stated below.
source_name: Abhishek Saha, “Large values of newforms on GL(2) with highly ramified central character”, arXiv:1412.5570 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5570

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2014).

title: Cavers et al.'s maximum skew-spectral radius conjecture for odd-cycle graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph with no even cycle, called an **odd-cycle graph**, and let $\rho_s(G)$ denote its maximum skew-spectral radius. For each positive integer $n$, let $H_n$ be the odd-cycle graph of order $n$ with one vertex of degree $n-1$ and size

$$
m=\left\lfloor\frac{3(n-1)}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

**Cavers et al.'s conjecture.** If $G$ is an odd-cycle graph of order $n$, then

$$
\rho_s(G)\leq\rho_s(H_n),
$$

and equality holds if and only if $G\cong H_n$. The equivalent formulation replaces $\rho_s(G)$ by the maximum matching root $t(G)$. The conjecture asks for the unique extremal graph, up to isomorphism, among odd-cycle graphs of fixed order.
source_name: Xiaolin Chen, Xueliang Li and Huishu Lian, “Solution to a conjecture on the maximum skew-spectral radius of odd-cycle graphs”, arXiv:1412.5727 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5727

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2014); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)
